svg.text: 108 datasets · 769,168 rows · 6 seasons. No lookup tables - each table carries its own identifiers. Key fields carry a coloured bar; type and an example value sit beside each one. Lines are routed through clear lanes and never cross a table.
one row per club per season
no Row_Type - every row is data
one row per club per season
some carry LgAvg / LgTot rows - filter them
team-scoped: a traded player appears once per club
Pos is a BR code string here, NOT a join key
identical grain to Standard - a safe 1:1 join
league-wide: a traded player has ONE row, Team = 2TM/3TM
those rows will not match a team-scoped table - by design
the name column is Name here, Player elsewhere
voting tables carry Name and Tm as well as Player_ID
one row per player PER POSITION per season
values: P C 1B 2B 3B SS LF CF RF OF
column sets differ by position - do not union blindly
two rows per game, one per club: 13,046 distinct games
the game-number column is named Gm#, not Game_Num
Player is a SURNAME only - never join on it
one row per fielding position per team-game
values: P C 1B 2B 3B SS LF CF RF DH
Franchise code, 2-3 chars. 2TM/3TM appears on league-wide tables only.
Stable Baseball-Reference id. The only safe person key.
Value sets differ: fielding has OF, lineups have DH.
Team game number. 163 occurs - makeup and tie-break games.
Same concept as Gm#, different spelling.
Identifies the GAME. 13,046 distinct, each on two rows.
Filter to data before joining or totalling.
any player table to any team table
ON a.Season = b.Season AND a.Team = b.Team
player table to player table (Standard + Value + Advanced)
ON a.Season = b.Season AND a.Team = b.Team AND a.Player_ID = b.Player_ID
fielding to player table (aggregate fielding first)
ON a.Season = b.Season AND a.Team = b.Team AND a.Player_ID = b.Player_ID
lineups to schedule (the column names differ)
ON a.Season = b.Season AND a.Team = b.Team AND a.Game_Num = b."Gm#"
both clubs in the same game
ON a.Boxscore_URL = b.Boxscore_URL AND a.Team <> b.Team
ON a.Season = b.Season AND a.Team = b.Team AND a.Player_ID = b.Player_ID
the schedule calls it Gm#, the lineup tables Game_Num.
Same meaning. Quote "Gm#" in SQL - the # needs escaping.
Standard_Fielding_By_Position uses OF and has no DH.
Defensive_Lineups uses DH and has no OF. An inner join on
Position between the two silently drops both.
team-page tables use Player, league-page tables Name.
In the lineup tables Player is a SURNAME only ("Ortiz").
Join on Player_ID, never on any name column.
Pos on batting tables is a code string like */3.
It is not a position key. Only Position is joinable.
some tables carry both. Team is the clean code; join on it.
Four things that will silently corrupt a result
102 of 108 tables end with footer rows - Team Totals,
Non-Pitcher Totals, Rank in 2 AL. Filter Row_Type = data first,
or the club counts twice: as its players and as the total.
Standard and Value split a traded
player one row per club; Advanced gives ONE row, Team = 2TM.
Union them and he counts twice; inner-join and the 2TM row drops.
Fielding is one row per player PER POSITION. Joined to
batting unaggregated it multiplies the batting line by his
position count. Aggregate, or filter to one Position, first.
OAK to ATH 2025. Group on the code pair, not Team alone.
N:1 many-to-one. Arrows point many to one.
Lines run only in the clear lanes between and below the tables.
Generated from the data. Every column of every table: 1_Source_Data_CSV/FIELD_REFERENCE.md and 2_Excel_Workbooks/FIELD_REFERENCE.md
